paragraphs: He belonged to the sect described here as “the known ones” and was a physician in Caesarea, as in Avodah Zarah 28a. He treated R' Abbahu, who would have been endangered had R' Ami and R' Assi not intervened.[^1][^2]

notes.text: מכת הידועים is literally sect of the known ones; its euphemistic/possibly censored connection to minim is interpretive, without assigning a religion. Mina’ah remains a transliterated sectarian epithet, not a canonical personal/religious binding.

כח. gives 28a conventionally. The prior consulted paragraph is reported to name Yaakov and Abbahu as the endangered patient, with a leg detail not inserted into Hyman’s text. No fresh check is claimed here. The source’s pronoun is implicit but Abbahu is the natural patient; the counterfactual and two helpers remain. All three abbreviated personal titles remain R'.
